cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 37th District since 2023. Previously served in the California State Senate (2021–2022) and State Assembly (2018–2021), and as president of the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees. Earlier worked as district director for Holly Mitchell and in nonprofits.

controversies.text: Federal records show $5,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021.
Missed 22 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (3.3%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 5, 2025-06-05 to 2025-06-06.

At an April 1, 2025 House subcommittee hearing, Kamlager-Dove said Republicans were "elevating a serial sexual harasser" as their witness. The witness was journalist Matt Taibbi, and she reposted the remarks online. He sued for defamation. In June 2026 a federal judge dismissed the suit, ruling her statements were part of her job as a member of Congress. The ruling did not decide whether the claim was true.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from her on data centers, new development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B visas, policing pay and pensions, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no state-level legislative actions on these topics in the pages we could read. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020 through 2026. Her place of upbringing is not stated in the sources we read, so we could not establish where she was raised.

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.bio: 27-year-old mother, activist and organizer from Los Angeles County. Appointed in 2021 to Santa Monica's Public Safety Reform and Oversight Commission. Ran for Santa Monica City Council in 2022. Ran for Congress in California's 37th District in 2026 as a Democrat.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended in four Sway voting-group guides: Abolish ICE pledge, Against Christian Nationalism, Jess's Progressive Picks, and We <3 Participatory Democracy. No organizational or officeholder endorsements are listed.

cands.gaps: We could not find her employment history beyond activism and a city commission seat. We found no documented stance on data centers, development or growth limits, property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of homes and land, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or policing funding. Her campaign names immigration reform as a priority, but the pages we could read give no specifics, and the detailed issue pages did not load beyond their titles. We found no news coverage or controversies about her. Her results in the pages we have are for the 2026 primary and general elections only.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign site says she was born and raised in Los Angeles County, grew up in Santa Monica, and moved to Baldwin Hills in 2022.

score.why: Raised $12.6k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Activist and organizer who ran guerrilla gardening and urban-agriculture advocacy in Santa Monica. She was appointed to the city's Public Safety Reform and Oversight Commission in 2021 and ran unsuccessfully for Santa Monica City Council in 2022. No elected office or paid career is listed.
qual.why: No elected office, legal, budget or management career is documented. Commission service and advocacy do not count toward the score, so she is a first-time candidate with a thin record.
